clue.text: I, possibly, poke chicken with a piece of wood

indicators.note: to poke something in is to push it into another thing, so the wood goes into the bird

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken
a log is a cut piece of wood

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to prodding a chicken with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the chemical symbol for iodine, and 'possibly' marks it as one example. 'poke' puts A LOG inside HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine, symbol I, is one of the group of elements that includes fluorine and chlorine, so it is an example.

clue.text: President, one gathering dust?

definitions.meaning: a vacuum cleaner picks up dust; the brand name is used in Britain for any vacuum cleaner

explanation.surface: A president described as a do-nothing leaving things to gather dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a US president's surname and a British generic word for a vacuum cleaner, the thing that collects dust.

clue.text: Something to set up, holding information primarily on enemy leader, cooperate

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so the first part sits on top of the last letter
holding means containing, so the reversed word wraps the letter
up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a sail is something a sailor sets

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter is taken
a leader is the one at the front, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An intelligence briefing on the enemy chief, with instructions to work together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SAIL to LIAS, 'holding' puts I inside it, and the result sits 'on' E.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep in contact and work in partnership with another group.

clue.text: Annexe where president maintains standard, not entirely beneath the state

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep or hold, so the surname holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant was the 18th US President

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue means placed below, so the shortened flag goes under the state

parts.note: NY is New York state

indicators.note: not entirely means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: An extension where a president keeps a flag flying under the state banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath' works because this is a down entry; 'not entirely' drops the last letter of the flag, and 'maintains' has Ulysses S. Grant hold the lot. A granny flat is a British term for a self-contained extension.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contained flat added to a family house for an elderly relative is a classic British annexe.

clue.text: Hot container lifted over bottom of potato chip

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above, so the reversed part sits on the final letter
lifted in a down clue means raised up, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a can is a container

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its final letter

explanation.surface: A hot tin raised above a potato that's fried into a chip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns HCAN into NACH, which sits 'over' O.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, served with cheese and salsa.

clue.text: Idiot finding ludicrous flaw in success

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters are placed within the word for success

parts.note: a hit is a success, as with a hit record

indicators.note: ludicrous suggests something absurdly jumbled, so the letters of flaw are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots a silly weakness in a triumph and dismisses its author as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ludicrous' gives the jumble ALFW, and 'in' sets it within the success; 'finding' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a common insulting synonym for a stupid person.

clue.text: A rest home prepared to offer beef substitute?

indicators.note: prepared suggests ingredients made ready in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A care home's kitchen readies something to serve in place of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges A REST HOME. The question mark nods to scandals where one meat was passed off as the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of the horse has been passed off in place of cow meat, a notorious food-fraud swap.

clue.text: Symbol of a nation, some ship capsizing

indicators.note: a capsizing vessel turns over, so the word is turned upside down

parts.note: the keel is part of a ship, its spine along the bottom

explanation.surface: A national emblem is part of a ship that has overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some ship' looks like part of a hidden word, but it is a part of a ship, KEEL, which 'capsizing' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is a national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Vital thing, having little room for big defeat

parts.note: water is essential for life
the loo is British slang for a toilet, the smallest room

explanation.surface: Something essential is lacking space, leading to a heavy loss.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British slang for a toilet, the 'little room'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final crushing loss in 1815 gave a name for any decisive defeat.

clue.text: Kebab served up during your old dirge

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the reversed word goes inside

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means presented upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a doner is a kebab of spit-roasted meat

explanation.surface: Someone sings a mournful song while a kebab is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses the kebab, since in a down entry up means bottom to top; 'during' puts it inside the archaic word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or song of mourning, the same as a funeral song.

clue.text: President Thingamabob, partially recalled

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so those letters run backwards
partially says only part of the word Thingamabob is used

explanation.surface: Someone can't quite remember the name of a president and calls him Thingamabob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes AMABO from inside Thingamabob, and 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was the 44th US President, serving two terms from 2009.

clue.text: Saw worker with president embracing writer

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was the 39th US President
a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: A man who has seen a tradesman, with a president hugging an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the tool; 'embracing' has the president wrap round the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner who cuts and shapes timber uses a saw as a basic tool of the trade.

clue.text: President no wiser, he stumbles past close of tenure

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the rearranged letters follow the single letter
the close of a word is its final letter
stumbles suggests something tripping and falling into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A president, none the wiser, blunders his way through the end of his term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close of' takes the final letter of tenure; 'stumbles' jumbles the three words into ISENHOWER, and 'past' puts that after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight D. Eisenhower, the wartime general, was the 34th US President, from 1953 to 1961.

clue.text: Country where I was a candidate

parts.note: to run is to stand as a candidate in an election, and ran is its past tense

explanation.surface: A politician recalls the nation where they once stood for office.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Very mysterious lord in bloody uprising, appearing common

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
in says the lord sits inside the word for bloody

parts.note: rare meat is bloody, barely cooked
Lord Lucan vanished mysteriously in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered

explanation.surface: A very odd aristocrat takes part in a bloody revolt and turns out ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody uprising' looks like a revolt, but 'in' sets the lord in rare (bloody) meat and 'uprising' reads RALUCANRE upwards. Lord Lucan was a British peer who vanished in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: The vernacular is the everyday local speech of ordinary people, so common in the sense of ordinary.

clue.text: Gerald's guards in that position with company, private

parts.note: Gerald's is read as 'of Ford', after Gerald Ford, the 38th US President

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it protectively, so the surname wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Gerald's is read as 'of Ford', after Gerald Ford, the 38th US President
there means in that place or position
C is a less common abbreviation for company than Co

explanation.surface: A security detail says the president's private matters are guarded by his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gerald's' is read as 'of Ford', after President Gerald Ford, and 'guards' has the surname surround the rest. C for company is rarer than Co.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said unofficially, not for publication, is confidential, which is the sense of private here.

clue.text: Dopey leader in Reagan, it being laughable for an actor

indicators.note: laughable suggests something ridiculous and muddled, so the letters are rearranged
a leader is the first, so the word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Ronald Reagan, a former film star, is mocked as a dopey leader in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets D, from 'Dopey leader', among the letters of REAGAN IT, and 'being laughable' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a performer specialising in tragic roles, a kind of stage player.

clue.text: Model put with Degas stole the show

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An artist's model posing for Degas outshone everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the noun, a sitter for the painter, but it is a verb that rearranges PUT and DEGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to draw attention away from them, which is what stealing the show means.

clue.text: Love left tainted if ends, unsatisfactory relationship now extinguished?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: the ends of two words are their final letters

parts.note: a lame excuse is a weak, unsatisfactory one

explanation.surface: A tainted romance ends badly, leaving a poor relationship snuffed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes D and F from tainted and if. The question mark flags a fire that has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: A former sweetheart is a love affair that once burned but has since gone out.

clue.text: Cheat knocking back a drop, happy to put on weight

indicators.note: to put on means to be attached to, so the reversed letters come before the weight
knocking back means sending backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a fall is a drop
up means cheerful, as in feeling up
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Someone who swigs a drink and is happy to gain some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' looks like downing a drink, but it turns the first three pieces round into PULLAFA; 'to put on' joins the weight after. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a fast one is an idiom for tricking or deceiving someone.

clue.text: Monroe unfortunately is as she is

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, Marilyn Monroe is in the state she is now in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges MONROE. Marilyn Monroe died in 1962, so she is dead: that is how she is.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead and gone is the state of Marilyn Monroe today, the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: A trail, an upward slope

parts.note: a scent is the trail a hound follows

explanation.surface: A walker follows a path up a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trail' looks like a path, but it is the smell a hound follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a rise or climb, a slope going up.

clue.text: President back in combat fatigues

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A president returns from war still in his military uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks TFAT sitting inside combat fatigues, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th US President, from 1909 to 1913.

clue.text: Good bandages nicer after treatment that's harmful

indicators.note: to bandage is to wrap round, so the word for good encloses the other letters

parts.note: pious means devout or virtuous, so good

indicators.note: treatment suggests something processed or worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A medical note: a good dressing makes things nicer after treatment, though something here is damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after treatment' jumbles nicer into ERNIC, and 'bandages' has the word for good wrap round it like a dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernicious describes something having a damaging or deadly effect, often subtly.

clue.text: Coax Nixon to admit lying in the end?

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: read as nix on, nothing on, meaning naked

indicators.note: in the end points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Persuading President Nixon to confess he was lying at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nixon' looks like the president, but read as 'nix on' (nothing on) it gives NUDE. 'to admit' lets G in.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge someone is to gently push or prompt them towards something.

clue.text: Second one sucks

definitions.meaning: a very short moment, as in 'just a moment'
a blood-sucking parasite that clings to animals

explanation.surface: A mocking verdict that the runner-up is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brief moment of time and a small blood-feeding arachnid.

clue.text: First in geophysics confirmed, so pleased

indicators.note: the first letter in the word is taken

parts.note: ratified means formally approved or confirmed

explanation.surface: A scientist is delighted to have a geophysics result verified.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratified means satisfied or delighted, a close synonym.

clue.text: Forget to secure ring that's likely to come off

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the word for forget holds the ring shape inside it

parts.note: to lose something, like a habit or an item, is to forget it
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to fasten a ring that is liable to slip off a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts O inside LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not firmly fixed is liable to come away or fall off.

clue.text: Perhaps one's kid gloves made from this?

definitions.text: Perhaps one's kid gloves made from this?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be in some other order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word are used, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a pair of kid gloves was made from this material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges ONE'S KID. As a whole, kid gloves might well be made from the soft leather of a female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is the soft leather from a female deer's hide, used for fine gloves.

clue.text: Serious attention given to tree house

indicators.note: given to means added onto, so the second part follows

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
a nest is a bird's home in a tree

explanation.surface: Careful attention is paid to building a house in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tree house' looks like a child's den, but it is a bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intention.
